title: Minimum operations to make character frequencies equal
spec:
You are given a string s.
A string t is called good if all characters of t occur the same number of times.
You can perform the following operations any number of times:

Delete a character from s.
Insert a character in s.
Change a character in s to its next letter in the alphabet.

Note that you cannot change 'z' to 'a' using the third operation.
Return the minimum number of operations required to make s good.

Example 1:

Input: s = "acab"
Output: 1
Explanation:
We can make s good by deleting one occurrence of character 'a'.

Example 2:

Input: s = "wddw"
Output: 0
Explanation:
We do not need to perform any operations since s is initially good.

Example 3:

Input: s = "aaabc"
Output: 2
Explanation:
We can make s good by applying these operations:

Change one occurrence of 'a' to 'b'
Insert one occurrence of 'c' into s

Constraints:

3 <= s.length <= 2 * 10^4
s contains only lowercase English letters.

bugs.description: When shifting to the next letter, treats the whole count as excess even if the letter keeps t copies.
Uses |c - t| as the shiftable excess even when the letter is below the target.
Never considers deleting a present letter entirely; only adjusts it to t.
Only shifts surplus when the letter is above target, never when it is removed entirely.
Only tries target frequencies that already occur in the string.
Never shifts surplus from y into z because the pair transition stops one letter early.
Caps the target frequency at half the string length, missing targets dominated by one letter.
